children: Zacks Investment Research has recently initiated coverage of
Volato Group, Inc.

SOAR with a Neutral recommendation. The report highlights the company’s expanding opportunities across AI infrastructure and aviation technology, balanced against ongoing losses, limited operating scale and financing requirements.

Volato’s growth profile has broadened considerably following the Sept. 14, 2026, completion of its merger with Alignment Engine. The transaction adds AI computing infrastructure to the company’s aviation software and marketplace businesses. The Ohio site already has operational power, water and water-treatment infrastructure, allowing development to begin at the equipment stage rather than requiring utility development first. Volato is now focused on engineering, GPU procurement, financing, installation and customer agreements, with capacity expected to expand in phases based on demand.

The company is also seeing traction within its existing aviation technology portfolio, as highlighted by the research report. Vaunt, its membership-based private aviation platform, reached approximately $4.7 million in annual recurring revenue as of June 30, 2026, alongside record quarterly cash sales and more than 2,700 paid members. Subscription revenues increased during the first half of 2026, reflecting continued growth from the platform. Vaunt also completed its first international member flight in July, expanding its potential market.

Volato AI provides another potential growth avenue. The platform moved into commercial deployment in August 2026 when Flyte became its first enterprise customer. Volato is developing aviation-focused AI tools designed to automate areas such as flight quoting, customer communications, crew coordination, maintenance scheduling and compliance. Broader adoption across aviation operators could provide an additional source of scalable software revenues.

The company’s shift toward a more asset-light structure also provides greater operating flexibility. Transferring fleet operations to flyExclusive has allowed Volato to focus more heavily on proprietary software and other growth initiatives.

However, liquidity and operating scale remain key concerns, as outlined in the report. Volato recorded a net loss of about $4.7 million during the first six months of 2026, while operating activities used $2.9 million of cash. Working capital was only about $0.9 million as of June 30, 2026, increasing reliance on external financing. Moreover, the sharp decline in aircraft sales has reduced the revenue base, while corporate costs remain significant. With no additional aircraft deliveries expected in 2026, software growth must scale faster to improve operating leverage.

Other risks could also weigh on execution. Material weaknesses in internal controls remain under remediation, while ongoing litigation may add costs and consume management attention. Vaunt’s growth is also sensitive to broader private-aviation demand, which can be affected by economic conditions, fuel prices, regulation and consumer confidence.

Volato shares have recovered recently but remain significantly weaker over the longer term. The stock’s relatively low sales-based valuation reflects subdued expectations amid the company’s financial and execution risks.

Volato’s expanding AI infrastructure, growing recurring-revenue base and asset-light strategy offer meaningful growth potential, while ongoing losses, financing dependence, limited operating scale and execution risks continue to balance the investment outlook.
